projects.name: Supplier Risk Analyser — AI-Enabled Supplier Risk Assessment & Comparison Platform
projects.description: Supplier management: Create and maintain a centralized supplier register, retrieve specific information and access assessment history. Document intelligence: Process uploaded audit reports, annual reports and financial documents to extract information relevant to supplier evaluation. Financial and delivery risk: Analyse structured financial metrics from CSV files and shipment/delivery performance data to identify financial vulnerabilities and operational reliability issues. Risk scoring and comparison: Generate supplier risk scores and classifications using available evidence; compare two suppliers’ scores and supporting information to assess relative strengths, weaknesses and risk. Objective: Reduce manual assessment effort and provide procurement teams with a structured, evidence-based approach to supplier evaluation and selection. Technology: Python, FastAPI, LangGraph, SQLAlchemy, SQLite/PostgreSQL, Streamlit, PyMuPDF, structured CSV processing and Tavily (optional external research).

technical_details.overview: Technical deep-dive of the Supplier Risk Analyser: Streamlit UI -> FastAPI API -> SQLAlchemy storage -> LangGraph workflow -> deterministic risk scoring, plus a two-supplier comparison RAG. LLMs are used in only two places: financial fact extraction (gpt-4o-mini via OpenRouter) and the two-supplier comparison. Risk scores are never LLM-generated; they come from fixed thresholds in code.
technical_details.end_to_end_flow: Upload document -> chunk financial content -> store -> on assessment, retrieve and extract facts -> compute ratios -> score -> persist.

architecture.ui: app.py: Streamlit; calls the API with requests and an X-API-Key header.
architecture.api: main.py: FastAPI; Pydantic schemas; API-key dependency on every route.
architecture.storage: models.py: SQLAlchemy 2.0 on SQLite (configurable via database_url); 4 tables.
architecture.workflow: graph.py: LangGraph with 7 nodes; financial_evidence.py does the retrieval.
architecture.scoring_and_rag: risk_engine.py: pure scoring functions; RAG_chain.py: LangChain + Qdrant for supplier comparison.

tables.suppliers: id, name, country, category, website. Cascade delete-orphan to the 3 child tables.
tables.evidence_documents: supplier_id, filename, sha256, extracted_text. extracted_text holds JSON chunks (schema_version 2).
tables.structured_records: kind (financial or shipment), filename, data (JSON). The last CSV row is the one scored.
tables.assessments: risk_score, risk_band, coverage_pct, result (JSON). Full result stored; history returned newest first.

data_model_config_security.config: config.py: pydantic-settings reads .env (unknown keys ignored); upload cap 15 MB.
data_model_config_security.security: security.py: secrets.compare_digest on X-API-Key; 503 if the key is still the placeholder secret, 401 if wrong.
data_model_config_security.database: database.py: engine plus a get_db() generator dependency (session closed after each request).

api_routes.GET /suppliers and /suppliers/{id}: List (ordered by name) or fetch one; 404 if missing.
api_routes.POST /suppliers/{id}/documents: Upload PDF etc.; chunk and store; duplicates detected by SHA-256.
api_routes.POST /suppliers/{id}/data?kind=: Upload CSV (financial or shipment); stores the last row.
api_routes.POST /assessments: Runs the LangGraph workflow and returns the result plus assessment id.
api_routes.GET /health and /ready: Liveness; readiness runs SELECT 1 (503 if the database is down).

upload_pipeline: Size guard: reads max 15 MB + 1 byte; larger files return 413. Filename reduced to its basename.
_extract_pages: PyMuPDF page text plus pdfplumber tables (kept only if 2+ non-empty rows). Also supports DOCX, XLSX/XLS, CSV, TXT, MD.
Page filter: keep a page only if the FINANCIAL_TERMS regex matches or it has tables.
_split_paragraphs: split on blank lines, merge up to 2,200 characters, hard-cut anything longer.
Chunk filter: narrative chunks must match the regex; tables become TABLE text rows 'a | b | c'.
Store: JSON in extracted_text; the same SHA-256 for the same supplier returns the existing id.

stored_chunk_fields.id: First 10 hex characters of the file SHA, page and index, e.g. a1b2c3d4e5-p12-t0 (stable provenance).
stored_chunk_fields.text: Paragraph block (up to 2,200 chars) or 'TABLE' plus pipe-separated rows.
stored_chunk_fields.company: Supplier name; retrieval filters on exact case-insensitive match.
stored_chunk_fields.financial_year: Always null today (upload never passes fiscal_year).
stored_chunk_fields.section: First SECTION_TERMS hit in the page's first 1,800 characters, else 'inferred'.
stored_chunk_fields.document_and_hash: Source file name and full SHA-256.

technical_details.chunk_storage_format: Saved as {schema_version: 2, financial_chunks: [...]}. graph.prepare() json-loads it and fills missing company, document and document_id with setdefault.

hybrid_retrieval.step_1_filter: Only chunks whose company matches; optional fiscal-year filter.
hybrid_retrieval.step_2_dense: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, normalised; score is the matrix dot product.
hybrid_retrieval.step_4_fuse_and_rerank: Reciprocal Rank Fusion = sum of 1/(60+rank) over dense top-20 and BM25 top-20. The best 20 fused candidates go to the cross-encoder ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2, which scores (query, chunk) pairs; the top 5 are returned.
hybrid_retrieval.queries: analyse() runs 4 queries (liquidity, leverage, cash flow, profit) and merges by chunk id, so at most 20 chunks reach the LLM.
hybrid_retrieval.caching: The index is built in memory and cached by a SHA-256 fingerprint of the chunk list (max 8 cached).

fact_extraction_and_ratios.llm_step: extract_financial_facts: gpt-4o-mini via OpenRouter, temperature 0, JSON mode. Evidence is labelled [SOURCE n] with document, page and section. Asks for 6 metrics plus 2 reported ratios, each with value, unit, period and source. The LLM is told not to infer or calculate, and to omit what is absent.
fact_extraction_and_ratios.code_step: calculate_financial_row: operating cash flow and net income are copied as stated. A reported ratio wins; debt_to_assets given in % is divided by 100. Otherwise a ratio is computed only if both numbers exist, share the same period and unit, and the denominator is greater than 0. A provenance dict records every input.
fact_extraction_and_ratios.precedence: In analyse(), values from an uploaded financial CSV override document-derived values.

scoring_rules.financial_score: Mean of the available metric scores.
scoring_rules.delivery_score: Uses on-time, first-attempt-success, failed and damaged shipment rates against shipments_total.
scoring_rules.overall_score: Weighted mean: financial 40%, delivery 40%, evidence review 20%, renormalised over the domains that have data.
scoring_rules.bands: Below 25 Low; below 50 Moderate; below 75 High; otherwise Critical.
scoring_rules.coverage: Coverage = available domains / 3. Missing data is never treated as low risk.

langgraph_workflow.description: Linear graph of 7 nodes sharing a TypedDict state; each node returns a partial dict that LangGraph merges. run_assessment() invokes the compiled graph.

nodes.prepare: Load supplier, parse stored chunks, split CSV records by kind.
nodes.research: Optional Tavily search (returns [] unless enabled and keyed).
nodes.analyse: Retrieve, extract facts, calculate ratios, merge with CSV, score finance and delivery.
nodes.evidence_review: Placeholder: always score None, available False.
nodes.validate: Check score is 0 to 100; attach supplier, evidence and analyses.
nodes.persist: Insert the Assessment row; stores 0 if the score is None.

comparison_rag: The endpoint gathers each supplier's chunk JSON, CSV rows and the mean of all past assessment scores.
RAG_chain.py: Documents -> RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (500 chars, 50 overlap) -> OpenAIEmbeddings -> local Qdrant collection supplier_comparison_{a}_{b} (cosine).
uuid5 IDs from metadata + text + index avoid duplicate inserts on repeat calls. The retriever returns k = 6.
LCEL chain: itemgetter -> retriever -> format_docs -> prompt -> ChatOpenAI (OpenRouter) -> StrOutputParser.
Prompt: act as a procurement analyst; 50% weight to scores, 50% to evidence; never invent data; five required output sections.
known_limitations: Scanned PDFs have no OCR step, so no chunks are produced.
financial_year is never set, so the year filter is inactive and several years can mix.
Table text can appear twice (inside a narrative chunk and as its own table chunk).
evidence_review is a stub, so coverage tops out at 66.7%.
Comparison endpoint: adding a list to an empty string raises TypeError when one supplier lacks CSV data; the RAG ingests raw chunk JSON; scores average all history.
persist stores 0 for 'no score', so history cannot tell zero risk from no data.
Operations: create_all instead of migrations, SQLite, retriever cache per worker process.

availability: Open to remote roles. Notice period: 30 days.
